sections.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the correct FUTURE forms (Will / Going to / Present Continuous / Simple Present):

questions.prompt: A: What [gap] you [gap] (do) when you grow up? B: I [gap] (be) an acrobat in a circus.
acceptedAnswers: are / going to do / am going to be|will be
will / do / will be|am going to be
questions.explanation: going to: intention / plan for the future

questions.prompt: I haven’t seen him for a long time but I think I [gap] (recognize) him.
A: I need some tokens to telephone my friend. B: I [gap] (give) you some.
questions.explanation: will: offer / decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: I got the plane tickets. I [gap] (fly) on Sunday.
A: Have you got any plans for the summer? B: Yes, we [gap] (go) to Italy in June.
questions.explanation: present continuous / going to: plan or arrangement

questions.prompt: Don’t play with those matches; you [gap] burn yourself.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: A: Whose is that night dress? B: It’s mine. I [gap] (wear) it at John’s graduation party.
A: Why did you call your grandma? B: I [gap] (visit) her at the weekend.
questions.explanation: going to / present continuous: plan or arrangement

questions.prompt: If your passport isn’t valid any more, you [gap] (not / be able to) go abroad this month.
A: What are you doing with that brush? B: I [gap] (paint) my room.
A: Why are you wearing your anorak? B: I [gap] (go) out.
I don’t know the meaning of this word so I [gap] (look) it up in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: will: decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: Look out! You [gap] (hurt) yourself with that knife.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: A: I’ve got a terrible headache. B: Have you? Wait there and I [gap] (get) an aspirin for you.
questions.explanation: will: offer / decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: Mother: Your face is dirty. Child: All right. I [gap] (wash) it.
questions.explanation: will: promise / decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: What time [gap] the next bus [gap] (arrive)? B: 13 minutes later.
[gap] you [gap] (open) the door for me, please?
We’re early. The film [gap] (start) at 2:30. Why don’t we go and have something to drink?
He [gap] (call) the police as soon as he gets home.
questions.explanation: time clause: as soon as + present, will in main clause

questions.prompt: A: What [gap] you [gap] (do) with that dress? B: I [gap] (shorten) the skirt.
acceptedAnswers: are / going to do / am going to shorten|am shortening
are / doing / am going to shorten|am shortening

sections.instruction: Use the correct form of the FUTURE TENSE:

questions.prompt: A: Oh! You’ve got a ticket for the party. B: Yes. I [gap] (see) it on Friday.
questions.explanation: present continuous / going to: arrangement (ticket bought)

questions.prompt: A: Tea or coffee? B: I [gap] (have) coffee, please.
questions.explanation: will: decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: There isn’t any cloud in the sky. It [gap] (be) a lovely day.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: We [gap] (win) the match. We’re playing really well.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: The festival [gap] (last) for ten days.
I [gap] (have) a meal with a few friends. There [gap] (be) about ten of us.
acceptedAnswers: am having|am going to have / will be|are going to be

questions.prompt: Phil [gap] (come) round us tomorrow. We [gap] (be) at the airport at 9:30.
acceptedAnswers: is coming|is going to come / will be|are going to be
questions.explanation: present continuous: arrangement; will be: future situation

questions.prompt: Why don’t you come with us. I’m sure you [gap] (enjoy) the show.
That [gap] (not / cost) more than $50.
The museum [gap] (open) at 9:00 every day but tomorrow it [gap] (not / be) opened at 9:00.
acceptedAnswers: opens / won't be|isn't going to be

questions.prompt: I [gap] (pay) it back to you as soon as I get my salary.
questions.explanation: will: promise; as soon as + present

questions.prompt: The manager said, “We [gap] (have) the meeting on Thursday.”
acceptedAnswers: are having|are going to have|will have

sections.instruction: Look at Tom and Sally’s diary below. Then, use the PRESENT CONTINUOUS form to say what their arrangements are for this week, as in the example: (Example: Monday – go to the cinema → They’re going to the cinema on Monday.)
sections.contextText:
Monday – go to the cinema
Tuesday – visit Sally’s parents
Wednesday – take the car to a mechanic
Thursday – buy a computer
Friday – clean the house
Saturday – have a dinner party
Sunday – go on a picnic

questions.prompt: Tuesday – visit Sally’s parents
acceptedAnswers: They’re visiting Sally’s parents on Tuesday.
On Tuesday they’re visiting Sally’s parents.

questions.prompt: Wednesday – take the car to a mechanic
acceptedAnswers: They’re taking the car to a mechanic on Wednesday.
On Wednesday they’re taking the car to a mechanic.

questions.prompt: Thursday – buy a computer
acceptedAnswers: They’re buying a computer on Thursday.
On Thursday they’re buying a computer.

questions.prompt: Friday – clean the house
acceptedAnswers: They’re cleaning the house on Friday.
On Friday they’re cleaning the house.

questions.prompt: Saturday – have a dinner party
acceptedAnswers: They’re having a dinner party on Saturday.
On Saturday they’re having a dinner party.

questions.prompt: Sunday – go on a picnic
acceptedAnswers: They’re going on a picnic on Sunday.
On Sunday they’re going on a picnic.

sections.instruction: Fill in WILL or BE GOING TO:

questions.prompt: A: Why do you need so much sugar? B: I [gap] make a cake.
A: Oh no! I’ve left my purse at home and I haven’t got any money on me! B: Don’t worry. I [gap] lend you some.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: I don’t know how to use this mixer. B: That’s OK. I [gap] show you.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: Why are all these people gathered here? B: The Prime Minister [gap] open the new hospital ward.
A: Did you remember to buy the magazine I asked for? B: Sorry, I didn’t. I [gap] buy it when I go out again.
questions.explanation: will: promise / decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: What’s that on your curtains? B: It’s a stain. I [gap] take them to the dry cleaner’s tomorrow.
A: These bags are very heavy. I can’t lift them. B: I [gap] carry them for you.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: I hear you’re going to Leeds University in September. B: Yes, I [gap] study French and German.
A: Why don’t you tidy your room? B: I [gap] play football in ten minutes, so I haven’t got time.
A: How can we get all this home? B: I [gap] ask James to come and help.
questions.explanation: will: decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: She has bought some wool. She [gap] knit a sweater.
A: This problem is very difficult. B: I [gap] help you to solve it.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: Why are you taking down all the pictures? B: I [gap] paint the room.
I [gap] climb that mountain one day.
Look at that young man. He looks very pale. He [gap] faint.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: A: Why are you buying that spade? B: I [gap] plant some trees in my garden at the back of the house.
She [gap] get better. There are positive signs.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: I’m hungry. I [gap] have something to eat.
questions.explanation: will: decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: I [gap] be 38 years old next week.

sections.instruction: Put the verb into the correct form using WILL or GOING TO:

questions.prompt: A: Why are you turning on the television? B: I [gap] (watch) the news.
A: Oh, I’ve just realized. I haven’t got any money. B: Don’t worry. That’s no problem. I [gap] (lend) you some.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: Those clouds are very black, aren’t they? I think it [gap] (rain).
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: A: I’ve got a terrible headache. B: Have you? Wait here and I [gap] (get) an aspirin for you.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: Why are you filling that bucket with water? B: I [gap] (wash) the car.
A: I’ve decided to re-paint this room. B: Oh, have you? What colour [gap] (you / paint) it?
questions.explanation: going to: asking about a decided plan

questions.prompt: A: Look! There’s smoke coming out of that house. It’s on fire! B: Good heavens! I [gap] (call) the fire brigade immediately.
questions.explanation: will: decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: The ceiling in this room doesn’t look very safe, does it? B: No, it looks as if it [gap] (fall) down.
questions.explanation: going to: prediction from present evidence

questions.prompt: A: Where are you going? Are you going shopping? B: Yes, I [gap] (buy) something for dinner.
A: I can’t work out how to use this camera. B: It’s quite easy. I [gap] (show) you.
questions.explanation: will: offer at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: What would you like to drink – tea or coffee? B: I [gap] (have) tea, please.
questions.explanation: will: decision at the moment of speaking

questions.prompt: A: Has George decided on what to do when he leaves school? B: Oh yes. Everything is planned. He [gap] (have) a holiday for a few weeks and then he [gap] (start) a computer programming course.
acceptedAnswers: is going to have / is going to start
